description: Agent Capacity: submit a capacity allowance with its recorded use: the allowance with its name, the amount for the period (tasks, tokens, budget or another unit), its unit, the period start and end and any exhaustion date the records state; each use with its id, date, amount, unit and the reason recorded when it ran high; the date the allowance is read at; and optionally the multiple of a typical day above which a day counts as a spike (2 when left out). The signed report gives the allowance with the days in the period and the days elapsed, the burn with what was used, what is left, the share used, the daily rate and the daily rate the rest can carry, the projected exhaustion date worked out from the records with how far it falls before or after the period end beside the date the records state, and every spike day with its multiple of a typical day and whether a reason is recorded, and counts them, and names an overrunning allowance: an allowance used up before its period ends and a daily rate that runs it out before the period end; then spike days with no reason, a projection that lasts only within a tenth of the period past its end, a stated exhaustion date more than 2 days later than the records give and uses in another unit, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No amount, no period, no recorded use or no reading date leaves the burn unverified. This reads one period allowance’s pace: a treasury balance projected against a reserve floor is wever_budget-forecast-brief, whether a limit’s remaining room is seen before acting is wever_limit-visibility-check and how one cap is counted across agents is wever_shared-cap-check. Verdict capacity_burn_overrunning, capacity_burn_partial, capacity_burn_unverified or capacity_burn_on_pace. POST /api/capacity-burn-check. Reads the load and capacity records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Capacity reads an agent’s own load and capacity records and checks the load against the capacity that exists: work in hand against the stated limit, a queue against its target wait, concurrent runs against the cap, an allowance’s burn against its period, a backlog across a window, spare capacity against the reserve, the scaling plan against the burn, and admission at capacity against written priority rules. Beside it, the Agent Limits checks such as wever_limit-substrate-check read whether a limit sits in code or in prose and how it is scoped, changed and seen, while a capacity check reads the load itself against the capacity; wever_commitment-deadline-check reads promised hours against due dates, while the workload check reads the work in hand against the stated limit over time; and the Agent Triage checks such as wever_triage-priority-check read how queue items are ranked, reviewed and closed, while the queue, backlog and throttle checks read waits, size and admission against capacity. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-capacity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-capacity/.

stated_exhaustion.description: The exhaustion date the records state, if any, such as 2026-11-20.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

read_at.description: The date the allowance is read at, such as 2026-11-20.

spike_factor.description: A day above this multiple of the average daily burn counts as a spike; 2 when left out.

note.description: Why the use ran high, if recorded.

name: wever_capacity-burn-check
title: Capacity burn check
